newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO FREE PALESTNIAN GUERRILLA WITHIN DAYS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO FREE PALESTNIAN GUERRILLA WITHIN DAYS.

text.p: A Palestinian convicted for bombing a Pan American airliner will be freed from jail within days and expelled from Greece despite U.S. anger over the decision, his lawyer said on Thursday.
"I expect him to be out in three or four days and he will be expelled. This is a court decision and the Americans can't do anything to stop it," lawyer Spyros Fytrakis told Reuters.

The United States criticised the decision to free Mohammad Rashid after he served only eight years of a 15-year sentence for killing a Japanese teenager and injuring 15 other passengers in the 1982 mid-air bomb blast.
"We believe that convicted terrorists should serve their (full) term," a U.S. embassy spokesman said.
Washington is expected to put pressure on Athens to try to have the decision reversed.
"The court's decision was taken in accordance with Greek law and was taken as it would have been done with any prisoner. It can't be reversed," Fytrakis said.

Rashid, 46, was arrested at Athens airport in May 1988 after a tip-off by U.S. authorities. Greece rejected an extradiction request and put him on trial in Athens. It became a test-case for U.S.-Greek relations.
Rashid was found guilty of premeditated murder for planting a bomb on the airliner, which landed in Hawaii.

The Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) officer said throughout that he was the victim of mistaken identity. He was sentenced to 18 years in 1992 but his sentence was reduced in 1993 to 15 years.
Rashid wants to go to the new Palestinian entity but the PLO diplomatic representation in Athens said this may be difficult.

"Our borders are still controlled by the Israelis. If he tries to go to Palestine he may be picked up by the (Israeli) security forces and handed over to the Americans. We are also looking for another country that will temporarily accept him," a PLO official said.

Fytrakis said Rashid had served his time in accordance with Greek-U.S. bilateral laws concerning convicted guerrillas and there was no way Washington could put forward a new extrdiction request or arrest him on new charges.
